context: area: Overseer terminal editor and live controls
constraint: preserve current player, persistence, and runtime contracts
input: user reports ambiguous action names and placement
intent: Make every Overseer terminal action unambiguous by separating session editing, live selection, publication, taking off air, and deletion.
expectations: No session-format, player-transport, or terminal-runtime redesign.
approach: Reorganize existing Overseer controls by state ownership, add accessible local creation and take-off-air dialogs, and reuse the current activation, publication, and clear commands without changing contracts.

decisions.decision: Place creation, activation/settings, publication, and take-off-air in their owning list, selected-terminal, editor, and broadcast contexts.
decisions.why: Location communicates scope before activation and prevents durable and live actions from appearing equivalent.
decisions.rejected: One shared toolbar or menu-only layout.

decisions.decision: Keep publication as the only primary update action and relocate complete reapplication to an explained additional menu.
decisions.why: Publication matches the common live-editing intent while the broader capability remains available.
decisions.rejected: Remove reapplication or keep two neighboring update buttons.

decisions.decision: Use accessible application dialogs for named creation and mandatory take-off-air confirmation.
decisions.why: Dialogs make durable creation and player-facing interruption deliberate and testable.
decisions.rejected: Immediate creation, native browser confirmation, or conditional-only confirmation.

decisions.decision: Chain take-off-air confirmation into the existing unfinished-progress decision only when the coordinator requires it.
decisions.why: The dialogs answer separate questions while backend state remains authoritative.
decisions.rejected: Combine speculative decisions or silently preserve/discard progress.

decisions.decision: Preserve existing desktop, player, persistence, and generated contracts.
decisions.why: The feature is a UI clarity change and current explicit commands already provide every required outcome.
decisions.rejected: Add a generic UI dispatcher or new boundary DTOs.

decisions.decision: Keep reapplication behind a native details disclosure and use local accessible dialogs for creation and take-off-air.
decisions.why: This makes scope visible while preserving existing Wails command boundaries and keyboard behavior.
decisions.rejected: A shared primary toolbar and native browser confirmation.

decisions.decision: Use deterministic queued and deferred browser-fixture results for all three existing terminal commands.
decisions.why: Pending, failure, success, and decision-required behavior can be tested without changing production contracts.
decisions.rejected: Adding test-only backend methods or new application APIs.
